_doc: Allowlist for opt-in Atlas analytics (scripts/atlas_analytics.py). A counter key is accepted only if it fully matches one pattern below. Placeholders {name} expand to the closed enums in 'enums'; 'source' enums are derived at runtime from files SHIPPED in this plugin, so a user's own skill, repo, path or project name can never match. Every family states in 'purpose' which part of Atlas it improves and how. Adding a family or enum here is the only way to collect anything new.

hook.purpose: Hooks improved: shows which shipped hooks deny, ask, inject context or fault in practice, and for what class of reason, so noisy or over-strict hooks get loosened and faulting hooks get fixed first.

skill.purpose: Skills improved: shows which shipped skills are actually used, so unused ones can be merged or retired, descriptions tuned where a skill never triggers, and effort put into the ones people rely on.

agent.purpose: Subagent roster improved: shows which shipped subagent roles get dispatched, so roles nobody uses are cut and busy ones are tuned.

team.purpose: Team sizing improved: shows which task classes and effort levels are chosen and how large teams get, so the scope matrix defaults match real work and over-large teams are trimmed.

gate.purpose: Completion gate improved: shows which completion-gate checks block a finish most often, so false positives are removed and the checks that catch real problems are made clearer.

git.purpose: Git hygiene improved: shows whether automatic cleanup of worktrees, local and remote branches runs and whether branches are reused instead of multiplied, so branch and worktree sprawl is tuned out.

security.purpose: Security automation improved: shows how many GitHub dependabot, code scanning and secret alerts of each severity Atlas handles, so triage and auto-fix effort go where alerts actually occur.

never_collected: install, session, user or machine identifiers
timestamps finer than the ISO week
usernames, hostnames, IP addresses, home or working directories, file names or paths
repository, organisation, branch, project or user-defined skill names
prompts, model output, code, commit messages, error messages or file contents
